Transcript:
PRESENTATION
Sh V Srikanth 00:00:01 – 00:09:00 (Group Performance)
Starting with the consol presentation. Quick highlights. One was, of course, it is an
exceptionally strong quarter in a turbulent world and turbulence in macro, turbulence because
of energy disruption. It was an EBITDA of Rs.62,409 Crores, which is 24% up on a year-on-
year basis. This is the highest EBITDA that we have declared for consol and simultaneously,
the PAT also at close to Rs.30,000 Crores, up 34%. Again, all time high, and with this, we
crossed the Rs.50,000 Crores mark as far as PAT is concerned. So, O2C led the charge with
EBITDA up 68%. Of course, we benefited from the unprecedented tightness that we saw in
energy markets, downstream cracks, fuel cracks, all of them, that is the markets were there,
but the operational excellence is something that Srini and Amit will cover. The IPO was
absolutely a defining moment, making Jio the second most valuable company. It is
particularly nice that it follows Reliance, which is the largest market cap company, and first
day listing of almost $137 billion in terms of value. A lot of firsts, which Akash talked about.
Largest from size or subscription, QIB portion, retail, those records were pretty good.
On O2C, as you recall, we have been always talking about, we have been having this very
structurally positive view about this business. And when you see our results, it really
vindicates, validates what we have been saying in terms of what the market has been and
what are the opportunities in this market. And what is particularly impressive is that it came
on the back of significantly elevated OpEx, the kind of crude premiums that we saw, the kind
of surge in freight rates, insurance costs. So, it is all coming on the back of despite all these.
And we have talked about flexibility and again coming in useful when you see the kind of
grades of crude that we were able to switch from the Americas and from the Meds, being
able to offset the impact of Gulf and the premium ethane advantage is something Amit keeps
talking about. This time it is among the widest that I have seen ever between naphtha and
ethane. And when you think about that, and in the context of the new ship that we have, it
came in. So downstream has been enormously valuable for us. Of course, the price
realization is good. Important that you have to be able to run the assets in full capacity. Asset
is good, but if you cannot get the crude, it is a problem. If you cannot sell the products, it is a
problem. So, to overcome and run it from an operational excellence, that has been
particularly impressive. When you look forward and look at the tight global balance, if you
look at the structural supply issues that we have, so we are very, very constructive. So, when
you look at the first half of FY 2027 performance, it is in our minds tracking annualized
EBITDA well over Rs.80,000 Crores and I think this is something, it just tells you how the
markets are.
And on new energy, I just wanted to say that it is accelerating and we see the benefit,
earnings contribution definitely starting in FY 2028. So, we will talk through I do not have a
presentation this time, but we will take it as part of the Q&A in terms of the progress in each
of these categories. Just the updates on the consumer side, this we have spent a lot of time,

3© Reliance Industries Limited 2020
but so I do not want to go back in Jio, but just two, three points here with number of subs,
but 300 million 5G customers, 30 million fixed, and that is half of it is FWA. What is important
is. We are able to, in our minds at least, we see visibility of high teen growth for Jio, and
those are the points that Akash was talking about. In essence, it is about customer base, be
it home, be it mobility, be it enterprises, then the ability to layer a digital service on top of it,
and then, of course, because of ownership of technology, IP, the ability to access
international markets.
Retail performance has been, you would have seen the numbers, about 6% revenue
increase, about 10% lower on the EBITDA side. But this is something that we have been
consistently flagging, and definitely last quarter we spent a lot of time. So, the strategy has
remained unchanged from what we said in the last quarter. We have been building online
presence. It has been coming on the back of a lot of discipline. We have been trading off
short term earnings growth to build a very scalable digital commerce platform. And the cash
flow from our store business, in a way, is funding digital commerce growth. And the benefit
of all this will be seen through FY 2028 and FY 2029 when this conversion of this scale will
translate in terms of value. What is good is that we are seeing the early signs of progress are
pretty good when you look at online scale, especially on grocery B2C, that number is up 42%,
very impressive set of numbers. Also, the online share of digital, both in grocery and apparel
and footwear, there have been also very sharp increases. We like that kind of percentage
increase. And we will see this transition happening over the next few quarters.
In RCPL, the focus remains on building the manufacturing capability and the distribution
there. And media, as you know, we have the widest reach when you look at it from both linear
and digital. And we have a very, very disciplined content strategy. You would have seen it in
a lot of media about terms of how we have been approaching this opportunity. And so, these
are the numbers. I will not spend too much time except you can see that revenues up 28%,
EBITDA up 24%, PAT up 34% and even when you see it and all of them on revenues really
driven by O2C and Jio. And when you look at PAT, standalone PAT is higher and JPL PAT
is up 14%. RRVL PAT is Rs. 2,611 crores, that is lower on the back of the transition that I
talked about and this is the individual numbers. Rs.25,203 Crores in terms of O2C EBITDA.
As I mentioned, 69% higher, one of the strongest that we have seen, benefiting from the tight
fuel markets and the advantage of fuel sourcing. Oil and gas, almost flat, 2% lower. Digital
services, we talked about 18% higher at about Rs.22,200 Crores. Retail at Rs.6,120 crores,
overall 24% that we talked about. And the debt numbers are, if you analyze this kind of
numbers, which is what the column on September 2026 shows, that is about 250, but it is
about 0.47. So, the capex has been very much almost flat, similar looking capex that we have
seen over the last quarters. But overall, I just wanted to say that we are mighty pleased with
the performance that we have seen in terms of earnings. And importantly, in business like
O2C that is something that we do not think it is something that happens in this quarter. I think
the markets are fundamentally structurally changed, and therefore we are well positioned for
that. Let us see, as time evolves, that is why the visibility is getting better on that. With this,
I'm going to Jio platform just maybe because that was a separate listed company, we have
done it. So, as part of RIL, we just need to do a few slides, Anshuman.
